email.subject1: covering more accounts after the Atlas merge
email.body1:
Saw Atlas just merged under Verse.ai, unifying your digital and SMS AI under one brand. A bigger combined footprint usually means more in-market accounts than the team can realistically cover.

That's the exact gap we close: an autonomous AI SDR that turns buying signals into booked meetings, 3-5x more meetings per rep without new headcount. Your reps stop researching and writing and spend that time selling.

I built a signal play for Verse.ai off your hiring and tech-stack signals, accounts showing those tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Following up after the Atlas-Verse merger. Integrating two GTM motions is exactly when rep time gets eaten by research and CRM admin instead of conversations.

Most teams I see leave real lift on the table in their sequencing. Our built-in best practices alone tend to move response rates 50-70%, before any net-new headcount.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, 3 specific things I'd change to get more meetings from the accounts you already have.
email.body3:
One more, then I'll leave you be. Memgraph had the same problem most scaling teams hit: more in-market accounts than the team could touch, and hiring SDRs fast enough wasn't realistic.

With our AI SDR they booked $2.7M in qualified pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, no new hires.

Want to grab time so I can walk you through how Verse.ai's reply rate compares to other venture-backed AI startups, and where the gap to target sits this quarter?

I haven't heard back, so I'll assume scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter and close your file.
